item.statement: Flat maximizer unique via Fourier inversion of constant coverage

chk.evidence:
Source read: Morwani, Edelman, Oncescu, Zhao, Kakade, "Feature emergence via margin maximization: case studies in algebraic tasks", arXiv 2311.07568v2. The arXiv abs page says "Accepted as Spotlight at ICLR 2024". I fetched the full HTML and extracted the math from its alttext.

(1) Our averaging step (average the coverage over delta != 0 to get Gamma_1 <= p/(p-1)) is their uniform class-weighting certificate. Sec 4 proof outline: "We will use the uniform class weighting: tau(x,y)[y'] = 1/(p-1) for all c' != a+b". This is combined with Lemma 5 (class-weighted margin) and Lemma 6 (the max-min certificate). The second part of Lemma 6 says: "all points in the support of q* are on the margin for any maximum margin solution."

(2) Our equality/uniqueness step is App. F.3, "Proof that all frequencies are used". Lemma 6 makes the margin equal across classes, so they write f(a,b,c) = F(a,b) + lambda * 1_{a+b=c}. The 3-D DFT of the indicator term is "lambda p^2 if j=k=-l". They conclude: "Hence, when j=k=-l != 0, we must have f^(j,k,l) > 0 ... there is at least one neuron for each frequency."

Our proof uses the same argument: constant margin/coverage, Fourier inversion of an indicator, every frequency nonzero. Their Theorem 7 claims only (1) single-frequency neurons and (2) every frequency used by at least one neuron. It does not state equal amplitudes, although their decomposition already gives the same value lambda p^2 at every diagonal frequency.

What is new in ours:
- uniqueness of the whole flat amplitude vector y_j = 2/(p-1) in the reduced programme Gamma_1;
- this holds for any network at b = nu, via Thm universal;
- a one-variable inversion in place of a 3-D DFT.

The averaging-then-constant-correlation pattern also resembles Welch/simplex bounds (folklore). I found no citation that fits better than Morwani. Notes are in /Users/ruhaanrajadhyaksha/projects/grok/heracles/paper/litcheck/items/t12-dense-uniqueness/CHECK.md.

recommended_citations.why: Supports the averaging and uniqueness steps in app:dense. Lemmas 5-6 with uniform class weighting tau=1/(p-1) are the averaging bound. App. F.3 proves every frequency is present, using the constant margin and a Fourier transform of lambda*1_{a+b=c}. That is the same inversion argument; ours sharpens 'present' to 'equal amplitude'. The entry already exists in refs.bib; it only needs citing at the proof.

chk.recommended_change: Add this sentence to the proof in the appendix subsection app:dense: "The averaging step is the uniform class-weighting certificate of \citet{morwani2024feature} (Lemmas 5--6), and the Fourier-inversion step parallels their App. F.3, which shows every frequency is present in any max-margin network; in the reduced programme the same inversion gives the stronger conclusion that the amplitudes are equal and the maximizer is unique." Do not describe the uniqueness technique as new. The new parts are equal amplitudes and the fact that the result holds for all networks at b = nu.
